title: Conjecture 2 (Jaeger, Linial, Payan, and Tarsi)
statement_text: For every prime number $p$, there is a constant $c(p)$ such that for any $t > c(p)$ linear bases $B_1, \ldots, B_t$ of $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$, the union $\bigcup_{s=1}^{t} B_s$ forms an additive basis of $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$.
context_text: Jaeger, Linial, Payan and Tarsi posed this in 1992 as a generalisation of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem to higher dimensions, and noted its connection to nowhere-zero flows. Alon, Linial and Meshulam had previously proved a weaker version whose bound on the number of bases depends on $n$.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture in the special case where the support of every vector in each basis has size at most two (Theorem 3), with an explicit bound $t > 8\ell(3p-4)+p-2$ depending on the number $\ell$ of distinct shadows of size 2.
paper_title: Additive bases and flows in graphs

title: Antisymmetric variant of Jaeger's weak 3-flow conjecture
statement_text: There is a constant $k$ such that every directed $k$-edge-connected graph has a $\mathbb{Z}_5$-antisymmetric flow.
context_text: Graphs may have multiple edges but no loops, and a directed graph is $k$-edge-connected if its underlying undirected graph is. For an abelian group $B$, a $B$-flow in a directed graph is a map $f$ from the arcs to $B$ such that at every vertex the sum of the values on outgoing arcs equals the sum on incoming arcs; it is nowhere-zero if no arc gets $0$, and antisymmetric if moreover no two arcs receive mutually inverse elements of $B$ (an antisymmetric flow is nowhere-zero since $0=-0$). Antisymmetric flows were introduced by Nešetřil and Raspaud; a directed 2-edge-cut is an obstruction, and every directed graph without one has a $\mathbb{Z}_2^3\times\mathbb{Z}_3^9$-antisymmetric flow (Dvořák, Kaiser, Král', Sereni). Jaeger's weak 3-flow conjecture (some constant $k$ such that every $k$-edge-connected graph has a nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_3$-flow) was proved by Thomassen for $k=8$ and by Lovász, Thomassen, Wu and Zhang for $k=6$; this is its natural antisymmetric variant. $\mathbb{Z}_5$ would be best possible: in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ every element is its own inverse, and a $\mathbb{Z}_3$- or $\mathbb{Z}_4$-antisymmetric flow must give the same value to all arcs, impossible for two vertices joined by $k\equiv1\pmod{12}$ parallel arcs in the same direction. The paper itself proves this statement: for every $k\ge2$, every directed $\lceil 6k/(k-1)\rceil$-edge-connected graph has a $\mathbb{Z}_{2k+1}$-antisymmetric flow, so in particular every directed 12-edge-connected graph has a $\mathbb{Z}_5$-antisymmetric flow. Since there are directed 7-edge-connected graphs with no $\mathbb{Z}_5$-antisymmetric flow, the authors conjecture that 8-edge-connectivity suffices.
notes: Stated in prose as 'The natural antisymmetric variant … would be the following' without a labelled environment.
paper_title: Additive bases and flows in graphs

title: Conjecture 14
context_text: Corollary 13(iv) shows that directed 12-edge-connected graphs have a $\mathbb{Z}_5$-antisymmetric flow. On the other hand, a result of Nešetřil, Raspaud and Sopena implies (by duality) that there exist directed 7-edge-connected graphs with no $\mathbb{Z}_5$-asf, so 8-edge-connectivity is the first open case.
